ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
<image1>

Points $A , B, C$, and $D$ are distinct and lie, in the given order, on a straight line. Line segments $AB, AC$, and $AD$ have lengths $x, y$, and $z$ , respectively. If line segments $AB$ and $CD$ may be rotated about points $B$ and $C$, respectively, so that points $A$ and $D$ coincide, to form a triangle with positive area, then which of the following three inequalities must be satisfied?

$\textbf{I. }x<\frac{z}{2}\qquad\textbf{II. }y<x+\frac{z}{2}\qquad\textbf{III. }y<\frac{z}{2}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, B, C, D are located in order on the same straight line. Segment AB can rotate around point B, and segment CD can rotate around point C; after rotation, A and D can coincide at the same point above the straight line, forming a non-degenerate triangle with BC as the base and that coincident point as the third vertex. Reasoning: Because A, B, C, D are collinear in order, and AB = x, AC = y, AD = z, therefore BC = AC - AB = y - x, CD = AD - AC = z - y. The three sides of the triangle formed after rotation are respectively the length x of AB, the length y - x of BC, and the length z - y of CD. Since the triangle has positive area, it must satisfy the strict triangle inequality: (y - x) + (z - y) > x. The left side simplifies to z - x, therefore z - x > x, that is z > 2x, so x < z/2. Therefore inequality I must hold.

method.method_draft: Use the diagram to identify the resulting nondegenerate triangle whose base is segment BC and whose third vertex is the common point formed when A and D coincide after rotation. From the text, AB=x, AC=y, AD=z, with A-B-C-D in order, so BC=AC-AB=y-x and CD=AD-AC=z-y. After rotation, the sides from the new vertex to B and C have lengths x and z-y, respectively. Thus the triangle has side lengths x, y-x, and z-y. Since it has positive area, the strict triangle inequality (y-x)+(z-y)>x must hold. This simplifies to z-x>x, hence z>2x, so x<z/2. Therefore inequality I must be satisfied.

图像描述：图中 A、B、C、D 按顺序位于同一直线上。线段 AB 可绕点 B 旋转，线段 CD 可绕点 C 旋转；旋转后，A 和 D 可以在直线上方同一点重合，形成以 BC 为底边、该重合点为第三个顶点的非退化三角形。

推理：因为 A、B、C、D 按顺序共线，且 AB = x，AC = y，AD = z，所以 BC = AC - AB = y - x，CD = AD - AC = z - y。旋转后形成的三角形三边分别为 AB 的长度 x、BC 的长度 y - x、CD 的长度 z - y。由于三角形有正面积，必须满足严格三角不等式：(y - x) + (z - y) > x。左边化简为 z - x，因此 z - x > x，即 z > 2x，所以 x < z/2。因此不等式 I 必须成立。

method.method_draft: Interpret the rotation condition as a circle-intersection condition. From the image, after rotation the common point P must be off the original line and at fixed distances from B and C. From the text, PB=AB=x, PC=CD=z-y, and the distance between the centers is BC=y-x. For two circles centered at B and C with radii x and z-y to intersect at an off-line point, their center distance must satisfy the strict condition |x-(z-y)|<y-x<x+(z-y). Use the left inequality. Since |x-(z-y)|<y-x implies in particular x-(z-y)<y-x, simplify: x-z+y<y-x, so 2x<z, hence x<z/2. Therefore inequality I must be satisfied.
